title: Typed Error Boundaries
description: Type error boundaries and error handling patterns in React so you can catch, classify, and recover from errors with full type safety.

data.text: React error boundaries catch JavaScript errors anywhere in their component tree and display a fallback UI. Typing the errors they catch makes your error handling more intentional — you know exactly what can go wrong, and each error type gets the right recovery strategy.

Error boundaries are class components that implement `componentDidCatch` or the static `getDerivedStateFromError`. They catch render errors, lifecycle errors, and constructor errors in their children. TypeScript can classify these errors and provide typed fallback UIs.

terms.definition: A React component that catches JavaScript errors in its children and renders a fallback UI.

data.text: Define your error types as a discriminated union. The error boundary catches any error, classifies it, and renders the appropriate fallback. TypeScript ensures each error variant has the right recovery action.

data.text: Create typed error classes instead of throwing plain strings. This lets error boundaries classify errors precisely and enables the error to carry structured data — HTTP status codes, retry timers, or resource identifiers.

data.text: A good error boundary offers recovery options. For network errors, provide a retry button. For auth errors, redirect to login. For not-found errors, suggest navigating home. TypeScript's discriminated union makes each recovery path explicit and type-safe.

data.title: Error Boundaries Only Catch Render Errors
data.text: Error boundaries catch errors during rendering, lifecycle methods, and constructors. They do NOT catch errors in event handlers, async code, or server-side rendering. Use try/catch for those cases.

items.question: Why not use try/catch everywhere instead?
items.answer: try/catch works for event handlers and async code. Error boundaries are specifically for catching render-time errors that would otherwise unmount the entire component tree.

items.question: Do error boundaries work in Next.js App Router?
items.answer: Yes — Next.js provides a client-side error boundary via the 'use client' directive and React's error boundary APIs. Use it at route segments to isolate failures.

items.question: Can I have nested error boundaries?
items.answer: Yes. Nest them so a failure in one section only shows a fallback for that section, not the entire page. This improves resilience and user experience.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Error boundaries catch render-time errors and display fallbacks
Discriminated unions classify error types for typed recovery
Custom error classes carry structured data (status, retryAfter)
Recovery UI is typed per error variant — no guessing
data.takeaway: Typed error boundaries turn crashes into structured, recoverable events that users can act on.
